name: Bounded corpus distillation with two-probe enumeration agreement
description: Turn a very large, messy log or session corpus into a bounded structured artifact an agent can reason over, WITHOUT loading it all. The mechanism that makes this more than a streaming script is the pair of gates around it: (a) two mechanically independent enumerations of the population must AGREE before any streaming starts, because a naive glob once returned 11,335 for a population that is actually 708, and (b) malformed records are COUNTED rather than skipped, and the tail dropped by the token budget is written to its own ledger - a silent skip is a coverage lie.

corpus_roots.description: Roots to distil. One fan-out shard per root.

token_budget.description: Hard ceiling on the bounded corpus. The loop truncates by rank until it holds.

extraction_schema.description: The schema that says WHAT to extract; the distillation is schema-bound by design.

max_memory_mb.description: Streaming memory ceiling. Under pressure the budget shrinks; the corpus is never fully loaded.

rank_strategy.description: How the token budget picks survivors. 'none' means head-truncate, which hides the tail hardest.

second_probe_source.description: The independent enumeration. MUST NOT be a re-run of the glob - a re-run is not a second signal.

enumerator.description: Probe A: enumerates the population by filesystem glob over the declared roots.

second-prober.description: Probe B: enumerates the SAME population by a mechanically different route - an index, a manifest, or a record-count scan - and never sees probe A's count.

streamer.description: Streams one shard under the memory ceiling and extracts per the schema, counting every malformed record.

reporter.description: Writes the coverage report: what was seen, what was malformed, what the budget dropped.

coverage-honest.expression: malformed_records_counted == true AND dropped_tail_recorded == true AND coverage_reported == true

stages.title: Probe A - enumerate the population by glob

work_unit.title: Enumerate the corpus population by filesystem glob
work_unit.question_or_target: Count and list every record-bearing file under corpus_roots by glob, and record the exact glob used so the probe is reproducible and its blind spots are inspectable.
work_unit.evidence_requirement: the literal glob pattern, the root list, and the per-root file count, so a reader can re-run the identical probe and get the identical number
tests_required: a root containing a known file count enumerates to exactly that count
both-states control: deleting one known file must decrease the count by exactly one
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: probe B's author, who must not see this count before publishing their own
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:DAT-7301 emitted only when the artifact exists, parses, and records both the pattern and a per-root count; otherwise FAILED:DAT-7301 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to a different enumeration route; a third identical glob is not a third signal
work_unit.mechanism: glob enumeration - fast, and blind to anything the pattern does not match

stages.title: Probe B - enumerate the SAME population by a different mechanism

work_unit.title: Enumerate the corpus population by an index, manifest or record-count scan
work_unit.question_or_target: Independently count the same population WITHOUT re-running probe A's glob, and state which mechanism was used, so a disagreement can be attributed rather than argued.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a second signal must be mechanically independent, so it gets its own agent and its own route

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the mechanism name, the command or index path used, and the count - plus an explicit statement that probe A's pattern was NOT re-run
tests_required: both-states control: on a population where probe A is known wrong (a directory the pattern misses) probe B must DISAGREE
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: probe A's author, cross-examining after both counts are published
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:DAT-7302 emitted only when the artifact exists, parses, and names a mechanism other than the glob used by probe A; otherwise FAILED:DAT-7302 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then escalate: a second failing independent probe means the population itself is ill-defined
work_unit.mechanism: index/manifest/record-count enumeration - slower, and blind to different things than a glob
work_unit.not_a_duplicate_because: it is the SAME question asked through a different instrument; that is what makes the pair a corroboration rather than a repetition

stages.title: HALT unless the two independent enumerations agree
Stream each root under the memory ceiling and extract per the schema

body.title: One shard: stream, extract, count malformed

work_unit.title: Stream one corpus root and extract records per the extraction schema
work_unit.question_or_target: Read one root as a stream, never materialising more than max_memory_mb, emit one extracted record per input record, and COUNT every record that failed to parse with its reason.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: extraction judgement is substantive; the streaming itself is mechanical python

work_unit.evidence_requirement: records_seen, records_extracted and records_malformed must sum consistently, and every malformed record contributes a reason string - a skip with no reason is indistinguishable from a record that never existed
tests_required: a deliberately malformed record appears in skipped_reasons with a reason, and is NOT silently dropped
peak RSS stays under max_memory_mb on a root larger than the ceiling
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the reporter, who must be able to reconcile this shard's counts against the agreed enumeration
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:DAT-7303 emitted only when records_seen == records_extracted + records_malformed and every malformed entry carries a reason; otherwise FAILED:DAT-7303 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot: halve the memory budget rather than retrying the same allocation
work_unit.mechanism: bounded-memory streaming extraction with counted malformed records
work_unit.notes: one record per fan-out item, keyed by item_key; resume granularity is fanout-item and the barrier verifies the artifact exists before any digest is read

stages.title: Hard barrier - every shard must be on disk before ranking
Rank and drop until the corpus fits the token budget

body.title: One truncation pass - drop the lowest-ranked tail and log it

work_unit.title: Rank extracted records and truncate to the token budget, logging the dropped tail
work_unit.question_or_target: Rank every extracted record by rank_strategy, keep the highest-ranked prefix that fits token_budget, and write the DROPPED tail to its own ledger so the interesting tail is visible instead of hidden.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: ranking choice is a judgement about what matters; the truncation is mechanical

work_unit.evidence_requirement: tokens_selected <= token_budget measured by the same tokeniser the consumer uses, plus a dropped-tail ledger whose length equals records_extracted minus records_selected
tests_required: tokens_selected never exceeds token_budget after the final pass
the dropped-tail ledger length plus the selected count equals records_extracted (no record vanishes)
both-states control: with rank_strategy=none the ledger must still be complete, proving the ledger is not a property of ranking
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the reporter, who cross-checks the ledger arithmetic independently
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:DAT-7304 emitted only when the bounded corpus fits the budget AND the dropped-tail ledger accounts for every unselected record; otherwise FAILED:DAT-7304 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: fixed, two attempts: a second overflow means the ranking is not shrinking the set and the loop must exit on no-progress
work_unit.mechanism: ranked truncation to a token budget with a complete dropped-tail ledger

stages.title: Report coverage, malformed counts and what the budget dropped

work_unit.title: Emit the coverage report reconciling enumeration, extraction and truncation
work_unit.question_or_target: State what fraction of the agreed population was streamed, how many records were malformed and why, and what the token budget dropped - so a consumer knows what the bounded corpus does NOT contain.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the reconciliation is the honesty-bearing step and is not delegated to the streamer that produced the numbers

work_unit.evidence_requirement: a per-root table of enumerated / streamed / extracted / malformed / dropped counts that arithmetically reconciles, with any unreconciled remainder named rather than absorbed
tests_required: the report FAILS when a shard's counts do not reconcile, rather than reporting a rounded coverage figure
a root that was quarantined appears as UNSTREAMED, never as covered
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent adversarial reviewer in a fresh context who recomputes the arithmetic from the shard files
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:DAT-7305 emitted only when every root is classified as streamed, partially streamed or UNSTREAMED and the counts reconcile; otherwise FAILED:DAT-7305 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: none: a reconciliation failure is a finding to report, not an operation to retry
work_unit.mechanism: arithmetic reconciliation of enumeration against extraction against truncation

stages.title: A silent skip is a coverage lie - assert the honesty properties

impact.blast_radius: writes only under command-center/corpus/bounded-corpus-distillation/**; the source corpus is opened read-only

worked_example.scenario: Distil the 344 surviving workflow scripts named by BP-GEM-05 into a 120k-token corpus.
expected_trace: enumerate-independent -> probe_b_count = 344 via the run-directory index
probe-agreement -> PASS (equal); had the glob returned 11335 as it once did, this gate HALTS the run instead of distilling a phantom population
stream-extract -> 4 concurrent shards, 344 records seen, 341 extracted, 3 malformed each with a reason
bound-to-budget -> pass 1 selects 402k tokens (over budget); pass 2 selects 118k and writes 197 records to dropped-tail.json
coverage-report -> enumerated 344 / streamed 344 / extracted 341 / malformed 3 / dropped 197, reconciled

bp7.unverified: UNVERIFIED that the harness-corpus machinery transfers to the WORKFLOW population it was not built for; settling experiment = distil the 344 surviving workflow scripts and reconcile this coverage report against BP-GEM-05's index, which is a mechanically different count.

distinct_from.BP-GEM-05: that one mines for workflow TOPOLOGIES; this is the general bounded-distillation machinery any corpus can use
distinct_from.BP-MNT-06: that one decides WHETHER to snapshot a decaying corpus; this one distils a corpus it is handed
distinct_from.bp-dat-04: no cost tiers and no funnel - this bounds by TOKENS, not by spend
